# head/: building and aging the 3D head

Owner: Person 3. Spec: PLAN.md Part 3 (building and aging). Contracts: head files out (CONTRACTS.md).

Lives here: frame picking and MediaPipe segmentation, COLMAP camera recovery, landmark triangulation, fitting the MakeHuman head template and hair shape, painting the texture, the face-aging step (run on the Vultr GPU), grey hair, age shape changes, the prepared aged skin versions, and saving finished heads.

Based on [Punching Face](https://github.com/akashngb/punching-face). People's videos and heads stay out of git (.gitignore).

## Blend shapes the XR app drives

Every `head.glb` needs these morph targets (names exact): `jawOpen`, `mouthWide`, `mouthRound`, `eyeBlink_L`, `eyeBlink_R`. ARKit names (`mouthStretch_L/R`, `mouthFunnel`) also work. See `xr/head.js`.

## Building a head

One time: `bash head/setup.sh` (Homebrew Python 3.11, packages in `head/.venv`, the CC0 MakeHuman template and MediaPipe models in `head/models/`; none of it goes in git).

Film: a phone on a stand at head height, about 1 m away, even light. The person starts facing the camera with a neutral face, turns slowly all the way round (about 20 seconds), and ends facing the camera again. Keep the mouth closed. Use the original file from the phone (AirDrop "Options > All Photos Data" or a cable), not one shrunk by a chat app.

Build: `head/build.sh captures/<video> <name>` writes `head/builds/<name>/head.glb` and `report.json`, then open `/xr/?head=<name>`. About 100 s on an M5 Mac.

| Message | What to do |
|---|---|
| Only N usable views / Only N views show the face | Film again: slower, the whole turn, start and end facing the camera |
| Only N frames could be placed | Film again in even light, closer, turning slowly |
| Face points don't line up between frames | Film again with a still, neutral face |

How it works (PLAN.md Part 3, following Punching Face's method): MediaPipe masks and face landmarks per frame, COLMAP cameras (exhaustive matching closes the loop of the turn), landmarks triangulated with a held-out check, the template warped onto them (thin-plate RBF), the scalp pushed out to the outlines for hair, a texture baked from about 40 views, and the five mouth and eye shapes from MakeHuman's CC0 expression units carried through the same warp. Tests: `head/.venv/bin/pytest head/tests` (from `head/`: `.venv/bin/pytest`).
# xr/: the WebXR app in the headset

Owner: Person 3. Spec: PLAN.md Part 3 (showing it). Follow DESIGN-RULES.md.

Lives here: the three.js WebXR app for the Meta Quest browser with passthrough, the mirror frame, loading a head, opening the mouth and driving it from the audio, blinking and small head movements, blending aged skin versions, the sliders with hand tracking (controllers as backup), and the theme file from the design rounds.

## Running it

- Open `/xr/` on the live link (once the server serves it) or locally: from the repo root, `python3 -m http.server 8123`, then http://127.0.0.1:8123/xr/.
- Quest browser: "Start in the headset" enters passthrough AR; the mirror appears about 1 m in front of where you're looking.
- Laptop: "Start" plays in the page (for casting and screenshots).
- `?head=<name>` loads `/head/builds/<name>/head.glb` (CONTRACTS.md). Without it, a stand-in head loads from the three.js sample files (dev only; its licence isn't confirmed, so it's never committed or shown to judges as ours).
- `?voice=live` uses the `/voice` socket (CONTRACTS.md) and the microphone (Jeffrey's `/mic.js`, started after Start; the browser asks for permission). Default is `sample/greeting.json`, a Mac `say` line packed as contract reply messages. Rebuild it with `xr/sample/make-sample.sh`.
- Tests: `node --test "xr/**/*.test.js"` (mouth analysis, PCM decoding, the queue start-time rule, gaze). `node --test xr/` doesn't work on Node 24.

## Files

- `mouth.js`: audio frame -> jaw / wide / round (loudness and zero-crossing rate), plus smoothing.
- `pcm.js`: base64 16-bit PCM -> floats. `player.js`: gapless Web Audio queue with an analyser.
- `voice.js`: sample and live sources of contract messages. `head.js`: loading a head, blend shapes, blinking and sway, glossy and toned-down eyes that turn to look at the viewer, and the neck fading out instead of ending on a jagged cut.
- `gaze.js`: where the eyes point: follows the viewer with a short lag, small saccades every 1 to 3 s, at most 28 degrees off straight ahead. In the page, `window.uncle.debug.gazeAt = [x, y, z]` makes the eyes look at a world point (for checks).
- `main.js`, `index.html`, `theme.css`: the scene, mirror frame, Start button and caption (DESIGN-RULES.md).

# Plan: aging the head in the headset, then chart panels (Isaac / Person 3, xr/)

## Context
- It's Sat 16:28. The Quest test passed apart from one thing: **captions don't show in the headset**. The dom-overlay panel doesn't appear in immersive AR. Demo blocker.
- BUILD.md still has **"Visual aging: skin, grey hair, shape"** unticked (this is the "agify" task). Nothing ages the head yet: `head/` has no aging code, and the Vultr SAM skin model isn't set up.
- The next unticked feature is **floating chart panels**. Ethan's server already sends `{type:"chart"}` messages, and `xr/main.js` ignores them.
- **Sliders** are blocked: Ethan hasn't yet answered the slider-message contract proposal on the board.
- Entire is working. Recent commits carry `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers, and the brain and graph plugins are installed. Every commit below gets checked for its trailer.

## Approach: age the head in the headset, no rebuild
All in xr/, and it works on every saved head (including `isaac`). One age number drives skin, hair and shape together, so a slider can later change it every frame (PLAN.md's "instant sliders" without making 10 skin versions first). The SAM skin model on Vultr can come later as an upgrade.

The head's skin, scalp and hair are one mesh with one texture (`material.name === "skin"`, head/uncle_head/assemble.py). The eyes are separate meshes (`eye_l`/`eye_r`). Their centres give a face coordinate frame: origin between the eyes, unit = distance between the eyes. All the masks below use that frame, so they fit any head.

New `xr/age.js` (plain functions, unit-tested) plus a shader hook in `xr/head.js`:
1. **Strength** `ageStrength(age)`: 0 at 25, 1 at 85, smooth curve. Used for the look only; Uncle never speaks it.
2. **Grey hair**: hair mask = (above the brow line, or behind the ears, using the face frame) × (texture pixel darker than the skin tone, where the skin tone is sampled from the cheek area of the texture once at load). Inside the mask: desaturate, lighten and mix toward warm grey by strength.
3. **Skin**: slight desaturation and sallow tint, faint procedural age spots (noise), and wrinkle lines as a normal tweak in fixed zones of the face frame (forehead lines, crow's feet, lines from nose to mouth corners). All scaled by strength and kept modest (PLAN.md: only one part aged looks creepy, so all three move together).
4. **Shape**: a small downward shift of the lower face and jowls, and thinner lips, in the vertex shader after the morph targets, so the mouth still animates.
5. **Shader hook**: merge with the existing `fadeNeck` `onBeforeCompile` (one hook, not two), with uniforms `uAge`, `uFaceOrigin`, `uFaceUnit`, `uSkinTone`. `head.setAge(apparentAge)` updates the uniforms with no recompile.
6. **Where the age comes from**: `?age=` in the URL (default 70) for now. When Ethan adds a server message with `apparent_age_at_70` (and slider results), it plugs straight into `setAge`.
